subject: Access & Erasure: batch retrieval for consolidated customer request
messages:
From: Daniel Mercer <daniel.mercer@acme-corp.com>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
Cc: privacy@acme-corp.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Bulk DSAR (Access + Erasure) — multiple user IDs

Hi Aisha,

We need Redwood's help to fulfill a combined access and deletion request for 14 end users across our tenant (Acme Corp). I've attached a CSV with the account IDs and request types (access/delete). We need: 1) a manifest listing all data types held (logs, embeddings, transcripts, metadata), 2) per-user timelines for extraction and deletion, and 3) confirmation of controller vs processor responsibilities for each data category.

Can you confirm whether Redwood will act solely as processor for data stored by Acme, and if so, what evidence we can provide to our data protection officer (DPO) to show exports and deletion proofs (audit logs, export bundles, deletion-commit confirmations)? We have a 10-business-day deadline from the first notice (starting today).

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Mercer
Privacy Lead — Acme Corp
attachments: acme_dsr_batch_list.csv (csv)
From: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
To: Daniel Mercer <daniel.mercer@acme-corp.com>
Cc: privacy@acme-corp.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bulk DSAR (Access + Erasure) — multiple user IDs

Daniel —

Thanks for the CSV and heads up. We're on it. Quick answers up front:
- For customer accounts where Acme controls the account and supplies the data, Redwood is the processor.
- We can provide per-user export bundles and a deletion proof package (signed manifest + audit log entries) suitable for DPO review.

Neha (Privacy) and Rishi (Ops) are looped in to coordinate the export/deletion run and SLA commitments. We'll confirm a timeline and send an evidence manifest PDF once exports are ready.

Next steps:
1) Neha — can you validate the CSV mapping and confirm whether any of the listed IDs look like service accounts or API keys we should treat differently?
2) Rishi — please prepare a preliminary export plan (estimated time per user, expected token counts, any KV cache snapshots needed).

I'll follow up with a scheduled 30-minute call if needed. If you have a preference for a DoS-safe export window, let us know.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Daniel Mercer <daniel.mercer@acme-corp.com>, privacy@acme-corp.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Bulk DSAR (Access + Erasure) — multiple user IDs

Thanks — I validated the CSV and flagged 2 rows that map to service accounts (user_0009, user_0012). Those will require a slightly different handling and additional justification from Acme if they request deletion (because they may be tied to integrations/backups).

Operational notes for the team:
- We will treat Redwood as processor for exported customer content (logs, transcripts, embeddings) under the Acme contract.
- Evidence package will include: export bundles (per-user ZIP), a signed manifest (redwood_evidence_manifest_v2.pdf), and time-indexed audit log extracts showing data retrieval and deletion API calls.
- Deletion proof will be a two-stage artifact: (a) deletion request acceptance ID + timestamp, (b) subsequent audit lines showing final garbage-collection/physical purge where applicable. For quantized/hashed caches we will document the state and the policy used (retention window).

Rishi: plan below for exports and deletion run — please confirm ETA.
- Export run window: 6 hours per 50 users (conservative), we can parallelize across two export workers for this job.
- Expected artifacts per user: messages.json (chat transcripts), embeddings.ndjson, activity.log (operation timestamps), metadata.json.
- For deletions: run delete-by-user-id endpoint + record response IDs. We'll collect audit lines and snapshot TTL metadata before deletion.

Daniel — can Acme confirm the 10-business-day clock? That will determine whether we need to prioritize. Also confirm whether service accounts should be excluded from deletion unless Acme confirms.

-Neha
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Daniel Mercer <daniel.mercer@acme-corp.com>, aisha_rahman@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Bulk DSAR (Access + Erasure) — multiple user IDs

Daniel, Aisha —

Export and deletion run completed. Attached is the initial evidence manifest (redwood_evidence_manifest_v2.pdf) and a CSV of delivered bundles. Summary below: 

Summary of actions taken:
- Export bundles: 14 per-user ZIPs generated and uploaded to a secure, expiring S3 share. Link and perm info provided to Acme's privacy mailbox. (attachment: acme_dsr_batch_list.csv contains mapping + S3 URIs)
- Audit logs: appended lines showing export job start/end + object digests for each bundle.
- Deletions: 12 user IDs were deleted as requested. 2 IDs flagged as service accounts (user_0009, user_0012) were quarantined pending Acme confirmation; we did not delete these. Deletion proof format: deletion-accept-id, timestamp, and final purge log entry when GC ran.
- Controller/processor statement: Redwood confirms processor role for tenant data held on behalf of Acme. A signed statement is included in redwood_evidence_manifest_v2.pdf.

Attachments: redwood_evidence_manifest_v2.pdf (PDF) — includes signed statement, list of delivered artifacts, audit log excerpts.
acme_dsr_batch_list.csv (CSV) — mapping file updated with S3 URIs and deletion status.

If Acme's DPO needs additional cryptographic checks (object digests, signed timestamps), we can produce SHA256 digests and a timestamped notarization file. Please confirm whether you want the service accounts deleted or retained.

-Rishi
Platform Ops Lead, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_evidence_manifest_v2.pdf (pdf), acme_dsr_batch_list.csv (csv)
